cells.tense: Many possible days are pulling at you, and how much you can hold is deciding which one you carry.
cells.ask: Give one whole day to one possibility and leave the others unanswered. Check on the second morning whether the pull changed. If it didn't, that's worth knowing too.
cells.core:
Several possible days are pulling at you at once, and you're steady enough to let the weight decide which one gets carried. Somebody mentions an offer and you already feel how the week would go — not idle, that's you catching a relation before it has a name. What keeps this balanced is that the biggest pull and the heaviest thing tend to be the same one, so what gets carried is what fits, not what shouts.

When it's going well: a possibility arrives, you take on its weight, you set it down when it's done. Nothing gets rehearsed twice. Nothing gets carried for somebody who hasn't asked. Bearing weight and wanting the thing are the same motion.

cells.tense: Before any of these days has happened you will have rehearsed each one, and you will be holding all of them at once.
cells.ask: Pick one possibility and give it today — the real conversation, the real move. Leave the rest unanswered until tomorrow. They don't have to be settled tonight.
cells.core:
A week ahead fills with possibilities and each one gets practiced before it arrives — the version that asks more than you have, the version that goes wrong, the version that quietly matters. Feeling what's coming is a real gift; that's how you know a room before you walk into it. Only it turns into a problem when carrying the days starts standing in for living one of them.

When it's going well: you pick one possibility and give it the whole of today. The others wait their turn without being rehearsed first. Nobody's asking you to stop feeling ahead — just to let today's load be today's and nothing more.

cells.tense: The pull toward what might be felt is still there, but the reaching for it stopped a while back.
cells.ask: Name one thing you'd want if wanting were safe, and say it to somebody steady — not the heaviest one. Then close the day there.
cells.core:
You can still carry what has to be carried — the endurance hasn't gone anywhere. What's quieter is reaching for things. Possibilities that used to pull at you now get a passing look and no second one, and hours go by where nothing new asks for your attention, because attention isn't landing on it. That's the shape being lived right now: strong bearing, narrow wanting.

When it's going well: one small want gets said out loud to somebody who isn't carrying anything of yours. It gives you something light to push against. Nothing has to come of it — saying it is the whole exercise.
cells.sheetLine: You still carry it all. Wanting things is what went quiet.

cells.tense: You are already turning toward some possibilities and letting others go, and it is being called just getting through the week.
cells.ask: Say one possibility you've been leaning toward out loud, once, while everything else is still being carried. Just say it, no plan attached.
cells.core:
Some possibilities are getting weight from you and others are quietly slipping, and the way you tell the week it's just heavy and you're just holding on. But the leaning is happening — one name lands differently than another in conversation, one option gets returned to when nobody's asking. Noticing that isn't the same as steering it, and yet the pattern is already there to be read.

When it's steady: you say out loud which way you're already leaning, and everything you're carrying stays exactly where it is. Nothing has to be decided. The lean just gets a name in the room.
